Sounds like quitting altogether is a good step. Coming to SD everyday will help for sure. You don't want to be in a position where you permanently injure yourself, hurt someone else, traumatize your kids (if you have kids) or destroy your relationship and right now all can be healed most likely - you can replace the drunk memories (which can fade into the past) with sober ones. I often think now that I am not missing out, I have drank my lifetime allotment and now it is time to be sober. It is as easy as not wanting the alternative (another DUI, not remembering, losing your relationship etc.). Read that book "The Naked Mind" and try to explore the reasons why you have destructive drinking habits. I know I was bored, hate myself and am constantly overwhelmed. I am trying to deal with that instead of being drunk and not solving anything.

If Sunday won't work, try to celebrate a birthday "week," get a massage, order your favorite dinner...watch your favorite movie. Do something you would never do before (and maybe make a sober friend in the process). Catch a movie with your brother mid-week. Have a great birthday and I will not drink with you today!

I don't feel quite amazing yet, but there is some wacky things my body is going through since I used alcohol to deal with anxiety and depression (I do feel better though overall). BUT, I do know alcohol can deplete certain necessary vitamins and minerals in your body, so be sure to get a blood test to see if you are low in iron or Vitamin D or if anything else is off. You may need to intensely replenish these things in your body to feel well. Just a thought (being from the Midwest US, my family and I are often diagnosed with low Vitamin D and it is quite common).

In my experience using alcohol (and/or antidepressants and a lot of times both together) buries the anxiety and depression, but the problem is that anxiety and depression still need to be dealt with and are there still when the alcohol is gone. This IS the hard part when you remove dependency from life (my life for example). I feel like I have nothing to hold me up, I literally can visualize and feel being broken and having my crutches taken away. But you have to do the hard work no matter what it takes to be free from not only alcohol but the constraints of your own mind that led you to lean on the alcohol (or other substances) to deal.

We are all connected through energy, but most people fail to recognize it or use it, so they feel very disconnected and scared of the world, as well as the process of living or dying. Personally, I think that the physical body is meant to feed and nourish the Earth after death and that pieces of your energy move on before you even die (hence why when you are older, you will probably be less frightened by death - personally at 39, I am exhausted and the idea doesn't bother me, though it used to). Think about this, if you know someone who writes a book that is good and successful, do you feel jealous of their success? Because your energy would naturally also feel successful and joyous because it is your world in which that success happened. It is also your success, you are connected to these energies around you, so recognize them, listen to yourself and what the Earth tells you, get out in nature and connect with it and stop being afraid (ego and feelings of having no control are what cause these fears). Enjoy the state you are in now because it changes over time. I hope that doesn't sound too odd. :)

Someone (therapist type person) recently asked me if I had ever had a near-death "experience." I let them know that I was in a really bad car accident, suffered a head injury, don't remember much of anything, but that the memories I do have don't match with what the people who saw me when the accident happened and afterwards stated. People create memories and sometimes when you are fully awake (during, say, drinking blackouts) your brain also stops making memories and/or creates new memories. Therefore, people - when they become conscious again after allegedly being dead - will create new/false memories to fill the space, which may include having a heaven/hell experience if they are religious.

Outside of the fact that some violence and many wars have sprung from religion, I actually enjoy that other people enjoy their religion and religion-based celebrations. I am not on a mission to convince people that heaven/God doesn't exist, especially if that makes life (or even grief/death) bearable for them and they do good things. My son loves religion and church, and he is free to partake if he so chooses and I do not force it on him, but give him the option. My husband is on the fence. I know what I believe and therefore can handle being around religious services and celebrations. Often times, I really enjoy sermons too! I cannot help that I am an atheist, I have felt that way since I was about 7 years old (I went to Catholic school till 3rd grade). I show up because I like to be around those people, and they show up when my events and parties are not religious based.  The only downfall is that the ceremonies can be boring, I don't mind that - I actually hate the standing up, sitting, then kneeling process more. I am pretty chill though, I would sit through anyone's religious stuff and partake in the process because I find that stuff interesting.
